findings.title: Crash persists after the vendor recovers: an oversized utilization is saved to 90-day history and replayed into Int() on the analytics busiest-day label
findings.source: Any vendor utilization field, e.g. Sources/AiTaskbarProviders/AnthropicWireTypes.swift:71 or ZAIWireTypes.swift:88, then VendorViewModel.recordHistory (Sources/AiTaskbarApp/ViewModels/VendorViewModel.swift:235,276)
findings.description: One response with a finite value of at least 9.3e18 (for example 1e300) sets snapshot.maxUtilization. recordHistory appends it to <vendor>.jsonl before SwiftUI renders anything, so the value is on disk even if the menu bar then crashes. compact() keeps samples for 90 days. AnalyticsStore loads 90 days of history (AnalyticsStore.swift:203). computePeakDay (AnalyticsAggregator.swift:29-47) picks that sample as the busiest day, and peakDayText converts it with Int() without a check. AnalyticsAggregator.swift:124-125 also feeds historyMax into totalUsagePercent when there is no live snapshot, and that reaches Int() at VendorAnalyticsCardView.swift:102.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) The vendor endpoint, or a MITM holding a trusted certificate, returns utilization 1e300 once. 2) The app appends {"max":1e300} to history. 3) The vendor goes back to normal values, so the menu bar and cache are fine again. 4) For the next 90 days, opening the Analytics dashboard computes the peak day and aborts the process, every time and after every relaunch.
preconditions: The attacker controls one usage response from any enabled vendor (malicious or compromised vendor, or a TLS MITM)
The user opens the Analytics view within 90 days
findings.impact: A lasting crash of the analytics feature that survives relaunch and outlives the attack. Recovery needs manual deletion of the history JSONL.
findings.fix: Clamp and finite-check utilization when UsageWindow is built (for example min(max(x,0),1000)), also clamp in UsageHistoryStore.append/load, and use a non-trapping formatter such as Int(exactly:) or clamp before Int() in the views.
findings.evidence: VendorViewModel.swift:229-235 sets state and appends history synchronously. UsageHistoryStore.swift:56-67 does no validation. UsageHistoryStore.defaultRetention is 90*86_400. AnalyticsAggregator.swift:29 is dayMaxes max(). AnalyticsFormatters.swift:46,48 call Int().

findings.title: Same persisted history value crashes the popover sparkline for 24 hours
findings.source: History JSONL loaded in VendorViewModel.init (VendorViewModel.swift:150-155, 24h cutoff)
findings.description: The 1e300 sample from history is reloaded on every launch. After the vendor sends normal values again, maxPercent (1e300) is more than current+5, so the peak label runs Int(1e300.rounded()) and traps. yFor() clamps for drawing, but the text labels do not. If the device stays offline and the bad sample is the last one, line 116 traps as well.
findings.exploit_scenario: After one malicious response, each relaunch plus opening the popover with that vendor's card expanded crashes the app until the sample leaves the 24h window.
findings.impact: The popover cannot be opened for up to 24 hours after the attack, across relaunches.
findings.fix: Clamp samples on append/load and clamp before Int() in the labels (the drawing code already clamps with min/max).
findings.evidence: SparklineView.swift:46 is maxPercent = samples.map(\.max).max(). Line 125 guards only 'maxPercent > currentPercent + 5'. VendorSectionView.swift:59-60 renders SparklineView when the card is expanded.

findings.title: Z.AI unit/number decoded as Double and forced into Int() inside the decoder, so the app aborts on every fetch
findings.description: unit and number are read as any finite Double and converted with the trapping Int(Double) initializer while JSONDecoder is still decoding. A value of 1e19 or -1e19 aborts the process before any snapshot exists. This is a different sink from the survivor: it fires in Providers during decode, not in a view. The 'schema' catch cannot handle it because a trap is not a thrown error.
findings.exploit_scenario: The Z.AI endpoint, or a MITM, returns {"data":{"limits":[{"unit":1e19}]}}. Each launch or scheduled refresh (300 s) decodes the response and the app crashes.
preconditions: Z.AI enabled with an API key
The attacker controls the response (malicious or compromised vendor, or a MITM with a trusted certificate)
findings.impact: Crash loop for as long as the endpoint keeps sending the value. CachedFetch decodes before writePayload (CachedFetch.swift:34-36), so the value is not saved and the loop ends when the vendor stops.
findings.fix: Decode with Int(exactly:) or guard the range, for example .flatMap { $0.isFinite && abs($0) < 1e9 ? Int($0) : nil }.
findings.evidence: ZAIWireTypes.swift:83-84. flexibleDoubleIfPresent (AppConfig.swift:199-203) accepts any Double. ZAIProvider.decodeSnapshot:58.

findings.title: OpenAI limit_window_seconds reaches Int() while the window label is built during decode
findings.description: limit_window_seconds is any finite Double. humanLabel divides it by 86400 and calls Int(days.rounded()) with no range check. toSnapshot runs inside OpenAIProvider.decodeSnapshot (OpenAIProvider.swift:171), so a value of 1e24 or more traps during decode. Utilization is not involved, so clamping utilization (the survivor fix) does not close this path.
findings.exploit_scenario: The endpoint or a MITM returns limit_window_seconds: 1e300. Every OpenAI refresh aborts the app.
findings.impact: Crash on every refresh while the vendor keeps sending the value (not saved, because decode runs before the cache write).
findings.fix: Guard s.isFinite && s < some bound before converting, or use Int(exactly:) with a fallback to defaultSpan.

findings.title: Overflowing model usage totals make the top-model share NaN, which traps in Int() in the vendor card (Z.AI and OpenRouter)
findings.description: Per-model usage values only need to be > 0. Two entries of 1e308 for the same modelCode add up to +inf, so totalUsage is inf and percent = inf/inf is NaN (ZAIWireTypes.swift:181-189, OpenRouterWireTypes.swift:169-176). Int(NaN.rounded()) traps when the expanded card renders. The survivor clamp on utilizationPercent does not cover ModelShare.percent.
findings.exploit_scenario: The vendor returns usageDetails [{modelCode:"a",usage:1e308},{modelCode:"a",usage:1e308}]. The payload is written to the cache because decode succeeds, and the app crashes whenever the Z.AI card is shown, including from cache after a relaunch within the TTL or as a stale fallback while offline.
findings.impact: The popover crashes. The payload is cached (writePayload runs after a successful decode), so offline stale fallback keeps crashing.
findings.fix: Skip non-finite totals and clamp percent to 0...100 when ModelShare is built. Format without Int().
findings.evidence: ZAIWireTypes.swift:180-189. CachedFetch.swift:34-36 writes after decode, and fallback at :105-108 re-decodes the cached payload.
